## Data

| File | Source | Used in |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `data/tourist_data.xlsx` | Statistics South Africa, *Tourist Accommodation* (P6410), <https://www.statssa.gov.za/?page_id=1854&PPN=P6410> | Projects 1, 3 and 4 |
| `data/usdzar_fred.csv` | FRED series DEXSFUS (daily rand per US dollar), <https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DEXSFUS> | Project 2 |
| `data/TSA_Part1_DataSets.xlsx` | Course data sets for Time Series Analysis Part 1 (electric knives, souvenir sales, strikes) | Tutorial: Part 1 Exercise 1 |
| `data/sales_data.csv` | Course data set: daily sales for several stores | Tutorial: TS Intro |

The remaining tutorials use data sets that come with R or its packages: `nottem` (spectral analysis lab), `Tbrate` and `SP500` from `Ecdat` (ARCH and GARCH lab), `marathon`, `oil` and `books` from `fpp2` (exponential smoothing exercise) and `usconsumption` from `fpp` (state space exercise). The state space and hidden Markov model exercises also simulate their own data.

The FRED file for Project 2 is downloaded automatically the first time that project is rendered and saved in the `data/` folder, so later renders use the same copy. All data are public, aggregated statistics with no personal information, so POPIA does not apply.

## Reproducing the portfolio

1. Install R, Quarto (version 1.4 or later) and the packages listed below.
2. Open the portfolio folder (or `portfolio.Rproj` in RStudio).
3. Run `quarto render` in the terminal, or use **Build > Render Website** in RStudio.

Computational results are stored in the `_freeze` folder, so pages are only re-run when their source changes.

## R packages

```{r}
#| eval: false
install.packages(c(
  # projects
  "fpp3", "readxl", "knitr", "rmarkdown", "patchwork", "rugarch", "dlm",
  # tutorials
  "tidyverse", "tsibble", "feasts", "timetk", "here", "forecast", "fpp", "fpp2",
  "Ecdat", "tseries", "fGarch", "SimDesign"
))
```
